facts.fact: Watch hours and subscribers gained through ad campaigns do not count toward the YPP eligibility thresholds
facts.kind: official (YouTube Promote help, quoted in search results; the page itself is not reachable from the session network)

facts.fact: Watch hours of ad campaigns, private/unlisted/deleted videos and Shorts-feed views do not count toward the 4,000 public watch hours
From 2027-02-01 new YPP applicants need 8,000 public watch hours in 365 days or 20M Shorts views in 90 days (with 1,000 subscribers); channels already in YPP keep their status
facts.kind: secondary (several outlets citing a YouTube announcement of 2026-08); to verify on YouTube's own page

facts.fact: Cost per view of YouTube video ads about $0.02-0.10 (up to $0.30 in competitive verticals)
YouTube's Promote experiment: subscriptions at about $4-6 each
Estimated ad revenue, Religion / US / English: long-form $198-528 per 100,000 monthly views (mid $330); Shorts $3.96-10.56

consequences: Ads cannot buy the YPP counter: the 4,000 hours and 1,000 subscribers must come from organic viewing.
Before 2027-02-01 the bar is 4,000 h; after it, 8,000 h for a channel not yet in YPP: reaching YPP before February halves the work.
After YPP, a paid long-form view costs ~$0.05 and earns ~$0.0033: ad revenue alone repays the spend only if each paid view causes ~14 organic views (break-even k, mid case).
The unknown that decides everything is k (organic views caused per paid view); it is measured by a small test, not assumed.
